newsitem.title: GERMANY: Meister - may know in weeks if euro will be stable.
newsitem.headline: Meister - may know in weeks if euro will be stable.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Edgar Meister said on Monday the French election outcome had changed the environment for Europe's planned monetary union.
He said it may become clear in the next few weeks whether the euro will be a stable currency.
Meister also said the monetary union project may enter "rougher waters" in the weeks and months ahead and warned that Germany must not lose its role as guardian of monetary stability.

"Since yesterday the constellation has been altered so that we might know in the next few weeks, not in 1998, whether the euro will be a stable currency," Meister said at a reception hosted by the state central bank of Rhineland-Palatinate and Saarland.
France's Socialists on Sunday won a resounding election victory, heralding a new European Union policy for France, less focused on austerity to qualify for a single currency.

"Germany must not allow its role as guardian of stability to be torn out of its hands," Meister said. "If the euro were to be a soft currency it would not have sufficient acceptance in the population."
